verdict: OK to lend in Halol auto components — pursue tier-2/tier-3 suppliers with diversified OEM books and EV-agnostic parts; avoid single-OEM, engine/diesel-specific, high-leverage borrowers.
title: Halol Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
Pricing power is thin on commodity parts and real only where design complexity is high — CRISIL notes diesel fuel injection systems carry high design complexity that strengthens pricing power [11]. So when a proposal lands, check which parts and which OEM; if the part is engine- or diesel-specific, ask about the EV transition plan, because CRISIL flags higher obsolescence risk for engine-related suppliers as EVs spread [11]. ## What has changed now
**National auto-component output is running hot — IIP NIC 29 at +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D] — but bank credit to the sector is growing faster at +27.0% YoY, a +7.8 pp gap [D].** That gap is the single most important fact for you: some of this lending is funding working capital and capacity ahead of confirmed orders. Gujarat is the brighter half, with GST collections +11.9% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D]. Peer results confirm demand: Motherson Sumi Wiring revenue +46.7% and profit +35% [4], Lumax beat Q2 2026 estimates and lifted its growth target [7]. But ASK Automotive shows aluminium squeezing margins even on record revenue [5], and Elara expects Q4FY26 auto EBITDA growth of about 21% with commodity risk rising [6]. Sources say little specific about Halol itself — the local ET pages [1][2][3] carry no usable operating detail — so lean on first principles and these peers. ## Where to grow
**Pursue tier-2 and tier-3 suppliers with two or more OEM customers, EV-agnostic products (braking, lightweighting, interiors, wiring), and a stated export or EV order book.** ASK's order wins span EV braking and aluminium lightweighting [5]; Lumax targets 20% revenue CAGR to FY2031 [7]. Avoid single-OEM dependent units, pure diesel/engine-part makers, and any borrower whose growth is funded by debt ahead of a purchase order. ## How to grow safely
**Structure as cash-flow lending against a borrowing base, not a clean term loan.** Take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, quarterly GST returns, and a covenant capping Debt/EBITDA at 2.5-2.75x — the level rating agencies treat as the outer limit [10]. Note gross current assets have averaged 160-170 days in recent years [10]; if a borrower's cycle runs longer, ask why before sanctioning. Collect from customer: exact receivable days, OEM-wise concentration, and hedging policy on aluminium and steel, since ICRA weighs hedging against profits [8]. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days stretching past the borrower's own history, inventory building without matching orders, and any shift in OEM mix toward a single buyer.** A Debt/EBITDA breach above 2.75x [10] or a missed monthly stock statement means stop disbursement and re-underwrite.

Margin compression without price pass-through, as ASK reported [5] -> ask for hedging policy [8] and stress-test cash flow
